state.rule: OperationalProcess owns strictly sequential revisions with at most one pending change; a change is accepted against the exact current revision; apply or cancel only for the exact pending change (root operation and intent); a cancel fences a later apply; a creation is refused when the identity exists.
state.decision: Retirement is a distinct terminal fact (planned OperationalProcessRetired) in the approved catalog. The event is not in code or schemas; the aggregate has no retire command. Today retirement exists only as a Lifecycle value inside revision content.
state.tests: Owner-level tests: replay of two applied revisions; second accept refused with pending; stale revision refused Conflict with no fact; creation on existing identity refused; revision on unrecorded process NotFound; apply with different intent refused and pending kept; second apply after commit refused; cancel then late apply refused; cancel with nothing pending refused; after cancel a new change is accepted at generation 2.

tests_cover_invariant.instructions: Do the listed owner-level tests together exercise the stated invariant of sequential revisions, single pending change and exact apply/cancel?

criteria.true: The tests cover stale, pending, exact apply, cancel fence and replay.
criteria.false: Important parts of the invariant are untested.

retire_gap.instructions: The approved catalog plans a terminal OperationalProcessRetired fact but code has no such event or command. What is the right disposition for this aggregate-stage session that may not edit schemas or shared catalogs?

criteria.add_to_model: Register and implement the event now in this aggregate.
criteria.report_event_change: Keep the aggregate unchanged and report the required event and retire decision as a needed shared change for the coordinator.
criteria.remove: The plan is wrong; drop it from the catalog.

retire_premise.instructions: Premise: the model text says retirement is a distinct terminal fact, while the code records retirement only as a Lifecycle value inside revision content, so a gap exists.

criteria.true: The code behavior contradicts the model text, so the gap is real.
criteria.false: There is no gap between model text and code.

cancel_then_accept.instructions: After a pending change is canceled, accepting a new change at the same expected revision with a higher generation is consistent with the rule.

criteria.true: Consistent: the cancel closed the pending change so a new one may be accepted.
